sentences.text: The Los Alamos Laboratory , also known as Project Y , was a secret laboratory established by the Manhattan Project and operated by the University of California during World War II .	Los Alamos	Los Alamos, New Mexico	University of California	University of California	Manhattan Project	Manhattan Project	World War II	World War II
Its mission was to design and build the first atomic bombs .	atomic bombs	atomic bombs
Robert Oppenheimer was its first director , from 1943 to December 1945 , when he was succeeded by Norris Bradbury .	Robert Oppenheimer	Robert Oppenheimer	Norris Bradbury	Norris Bradbury
For scientists freely to discuss their work while preserving security , the laboratory was located in a remote part of New Mexico .	New Mexico	New Mexico
The wartime laboratory occupied buildings that had once been part of the Los Alamos Ranch School .	Los Alamos	Los Alamos, New Mexico	Los Alamos Ranch School	Los Alamos Ranch School

The development effort initially concentrated on a gun-type fission weapon using plutonium called Thin Man .	gun-type fission weapon	gun-type fission weapon	plutonium	plutonium	Thin Man	Thin Man (nuclear bomb)

In April 1944 , the Los Alamos Laboratory determined that the rate of spontaneous fission in plutonium bred in a nuclear reactor was too great due to the presence of plutonium-240 and would cause a predetonation , a nuclear chain reaction before the core was fully assembled .	Los Alamos	Los Alamos, New Mexico	plutonium	plutonium	spontaneous fission	spontaneous fission	plutonium-240	plutonium-240	predetonation	Fizzle (nuclear test)	nuclear chain reaction	nuclear chain reaction	core	Pit (nuclear weapon)

Oppenheimer then reorganized the laboratory and orchestrated an all-out and ultimately successful effort on an alternative design proposed by John von Neumann , an implosion-type nuclear weapon , which was called Fat Man .	John von Neumann	John von Neumann	implosion-type nuclear weapon	implosion-type nuclear weapon	Fat Man	Fat Man
A variant of the gun-type design known as Little Boy was developed using uranium-235 .	Little Boy	Little Boy	uranium-235	uranium-235

Chemists at the Los Alamos Laboratory developed methods of purifying uranium and plutonium , the latter a metal that only existed in microscopic quantities when Project Y began .	Los Alamos	Los Alamos, New Mexico	plutonium	plutonium
Its metallurgists found that plutonium had unexpected properties , but were nonetheless able to cast it into metal spheres .	plutonium	plutonium
The laboratory built the Water Boiler , an aqueous homogeneous reactor , the third reactor in the world to become operational .	aqueous homogeneous reactor	aqueous homogeneous reactor

It also researched the Super , a hydrogen bomb that would use a fission bomb to ignite a nuclear fusion reaction in deuterium and tritium .	hydrogen bomb	hydrogen bomb	nuclear fusion	nuclear fusion	deuterium	deuterium	tritium	tritium
The Fat Man design was tested in the Trinity nuclear test in July 1945 .	Fat Man	Fat Man	Trinity nuclear test	Trinity nuclear test

Project Y personnel formed pit crews and assembly teams for the bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and participated in the bombing as weaponeers and observers .	bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki	bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
After the war ended , the laboratory supported the Operation Crossroads nuclear tests at Bikini Atoll .	Operation Crossroads	Operation Crossroads	Bikini Atoll	Bikini Atoll
A new Z Division was created to control testing , stockpiling and bomb assembly activities , which were concentrated at Sandia Base .	Sandia Base	Sandia Base
The Los Alamos Laboratory became Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory in 1947 .	Los Alamos	Los Alamos, New Mexico	Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory	Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory
